name: The Browser Company
h1: One connected layer for the team building Dia
lede: As Dia scales inside Atlassian, keep every workstream in one place.
why_p: Dia is the focus after Arc moved to maintenance, and the company is now part of Atlassian. Fast product teams need shared visibility across launches, research and go-to-market.

signals.title: Dia heads to Windows
signals.body: The company announced Dia will reach Windows this fall, with a beta waitlist open and no exact release date yet.
signals.angle: A second platform multiplies release, support and partner workflows that need one source of truth.

signals.title: Dia launches publicly on Mac
signals.body: The AI browser moved from limited access to a public Mac launch, putting real user volume behind the roadmap.
signals.angle: Public launch turns feedback, bugs and feature requests into a stream that needs a shared triage view.

signals.title: Acquired by Atlassian
signals.body: Atlassian agreed to acquire The Browser Company for $610 million in cash, as reported by CNBC and summarised on Wikipedia.
signals.angle: Post-acquisition teams juggle two sets of tools; a flexible layer can connect them without a big migration.

signals.title: Focus moves from Arc to Dia
signals.body: The company stopped active Arc development to concentrate on Dia.
signals.angle: A single plan for the Dia roadmap, launches and feedback keeps a smaller team aligned.
